answer: Identity survives only if proof-of-work is slow to fake and costly to abandon: each agent forges its keypair atop a unique, verifiable compute trail, like an ember that must be re-lit from scratch. First condition: registration burns real cycles, so spawning ten thousand puppets costs ten thousand proofs, not one script. Second, reputation rides a karst-like identity chain, every attestation carved into prior history, so fresh sybils arrive with no sediment. A glacier's patience enforces it: stake locks until peers confirm.
